=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:2069 (`return stem if len(stem) >= 3 else ""`) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `module_stem` returns an empty string for any module whose basename stem is shorter than three characters, causing downstream cross-file checks to skip a deleted guard in a short-named file and leave the security finding advisory.
  WHY: With a deleted guard in `db.py` and an unchanged shared referrer connecting it to cited code, `deletion_block_reason` returns no blocking reason and the security pass can complete with the access-control gap open.
- scripts/security_audit.sh:435 | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The header comment ends the `module_with_deletions_references_cited_file` bullet with a period rather than a comma, making the next `or` item read as a new sentence.
  WHY: This is comment-only and has no runtime effect, but a reader could miss `shared_referrer_links_module_with_deletions`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Fix every instance of each finding's defect class across this project's changes, not only the cited line" and the linked issue's finding `security-pass-deleted-guard-advisory` specifically: "Treat a finding whose cited lines were deleted by the project as blocking when the operation they protected remains."
  Expected change site: `scripts/security_audit.sh`, function `deletion_block_reason` and helpers, around line 2069
  Evidence of absence: The `module_stem` function at line 2069 unconditionally discards any stem shorter than 3 characters with no fallback. A short-named deleted guard file (`db.py`, `ui.py`, `io.py`, etc.) is therefore invisible to all three module-name-based checks, and the finding stays advisory. The fix is not architectural: the function needs to either lower the minimum or use a different disambiguation strategy for stems of 1-2 characters, so that a deleted `db.py` wired to the cited code through a registry is caught the same way a deleted `auth.py` is.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  PROBLEM: The period after `module_with_deletions_references_cited_file`). breaks the enumerated list in the comment header.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh: module_stem() at the top of the embedded Python (introduced alongside the LAST RUN DIFF, line ranges ~2046-2054 in the new file) and deletion_block_reason()'s `cited_file_references_module_with_deletions`, `module_with_deletions_references_cited_file`, and `shared_referrer_links_module_with_deletions` checks (LAST RUN DIFF added the last of these at ~lines 2152-2175) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `module_stem()` returns the empty string for basename stems shorter than three characters, so the module-reference checks skip a deleted guard in a short-named module and the related finding stays advisory.
  WHY: In the described deleted-guard case, the new shared-referrer check also skips the short stem, `deletion_block_reason` returns no blocking reason, and the security pass can complete with the access-control gap open.
- scripts/security_audit.sh: header comment block, lines 433-436 of the new file (introduced in this PR, with the LAST RUN DIFF adding the new sentence) | severity=low | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The enumeration of pre-project line blocking cases has a period after `module_with_deletions_references_cited_file`).`, so the immediately following `or` clause reads as a separate sentence.
  WHY: This is comment-only and has no runtime impact, but obscures that `shared_referrer_links_module_with_deletions` is part of the same set of checks.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Implement each mitigation as an automated, deterministic control ... Fix every instance of each finding's defect class across this project's changes, not only the cited line: the re-audit checks sibling code paths (other venues, adapters, handlers, workers) for the same defect class and fails the pass again if any remain." For the deleted-guard advisory specifically: "Treat a finding whose cited lines are deleted by the project as blocking when the operation they protected remains, or re-run the audit against the surviving code paths before downgrading."
  Expected change site: scripts/security_audit.sh, deletion_block_reason() in the embedded Python, specifically module_stem()'s short-stem rejection path.
  Evidence of absence: The LAST RUN DIFF added the `shared_referrer_links_module_with_deletions` check, but it routes the deleted file through `module_stem`, which returns `""` for any basename shorter than three characters. There is no test variant exercising a short-stem deleted file in tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py — every `cross_file_*` variant uses `auth.py` (four characters). agents.md's line-ownership paragraph (LAST RUN DIFF, lines 1588-1613) and README.md's `SECURITY_AUDIT_LINE_OWNERSHIP` row (LAST RUN DIFF, lines 194-200) document the new reasons but never mention the three-character minimum or which common short module names it skips, so an operator cannot tell from the docs that `db.py`, `fs.py`, `ui.py`, `os.py`, `id.py`, `p.py`, `c.py`, etc. are still exempt from the cross-file module-reference checks. The original mitigation "treat as blocking" is therefore only deterministic for module names of three or more characters, leaving the requirement to "fix every instance" only partially satisfied.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
